scope.reason: ValueError: engineering full service exceeded two seconds

clockMethod.additiveBoundary: actual outer sample start through actual full callback completion, with exact additive nonoverlapping segment sums
clockMethod.apiBoundary: Only API duration is recorded. It is a nested interval inside the preceding-reaped to after-graph envelope; subtraction labels the remaining mixed overhead, not API start/end timestamps.
clockMethod.nativeClock: C internal clock_gettime.CLOCK_MONOTONIC durations only. Absolute C nanoseconds are never compared with Python monotonic origins.
clockMethod.eventStamp: Lifecycle event monotonic is sampled before canonical replay/write/fsync; event-to-event gaps are bounding intervals, not isolated fsync measurements.
clockMethod.reapedField: ManagedProcess._reap samples reapedMonotonic after Popen.wait returned AND after identity lookup through Registry._lease; it is not an OS kernel reap timestamp or isolated target runtime.

majorFindings: The decisive refusal is the stricter complete-service >2 second gate at index9. All ten raw process predicates and raw outer validation statuses are PASS; the tenth callback refuses before phase validatedSamples increments. Whole observation remains below its separate 2.5 second limit.

The largest directly bounded segment pair is graph-complete to listener-ready. It includes native reparsing, exact daemon identity and whole-executable SHA reads, and managed listener preparation/Python-ready startup. The present raw clocks cannot separate those components.

The two C internal intervals are only milliseconds combined. Native managed-wrapper intervals contain Python-ready launch, identity checks, registration/release/wait journaling, I/O, cleanup and C execution; neither wrapper nor graph envelope is pure C time.

Post-unlock guard, outer validation and output writers are smaller on these ten short prefixes. The first post-unlock and outer-validation intervals are higher than the last; the retained prefix range does not support claiming that full-prefix replay growth caused this refusal.

The final versus first full-service delta is arithmetically concentrated in the mixed graph-complete/listener-ready envelopes. This is an observed interval difference, not causal attribution to daemon hashing, site initialization, filesystem effects or journal length.

daemonHashCandidate.factBoundary: Sizes are post-stop stat metadata for policy-bound paths, not new binary-content authentication or a measured per-hash duration. Frozen source performs complete app and serve SHA reads in each of two snapshots; no stat-only optimization is proposed.

shimAssessment.mechanism: The frozen shim uses only standard-library modules. Its actual interpreter argv includes -B and no -S, so standard site initialization is enabled. Local CPython 3.12 site.py documents automatic site-path/.pth/customize processing unless -S. Its actual duration and active customization effects were not profiled.
shimAssessment.targetBoundary: A narrowly implemented -S change would affect the interpreter running only lifecycle_exec.py. Preserve os.execve(command[0],command,dict(os.environ)), target argv suffix and environment passed by Registry; do not add -S to a Python target command or set interpreter/environment suppression variables globally.
shimAssessment.potentialBenefit: Plausible reduction of ready-handshake startup work for each native/listener task, but magnitude and full-load sufficiency are UNKNOWN. Native graph-start-to-ready is only an upper envelope on native startup; listener startup has no isolated begin clock.
uncertainties: No successful launchStarted timestamp is recorded; ready/registration/release/reap clocks do not isolate interpreter startup.

Inherited sitecustomize/usercustomize/.pth environment side effects were not inspected. Skipping site may change those effects, so target effective argv/environment equivalence must be explicitly demonstrated with a controlled dictionary.
The largest mixed segment also contains complete daemon executable hashing; -S cannot remove that required content-authentication cost.
Ten stopped prefixes are not the declared full equivalent load and cannot establish future long-ledger service or qualification feasibility.
proposedOfflineThenBoundedEngineeringCon: Pure argv construction test: -S/-B apply only before the shim script; target command list stays byte-identical.
Controlled disposable target captures exact argv and explicitly supplied nonsecret environment for baseline versus -S shim; verify target receives the same values and no flags leak.
Same PID, parent PID, held-gate two kernel birth reads, exact source/executable bindings, empty native argv, release, actual parent wait and cleanup/refusal controls retained.
Explicit ready timeout, malformed/oversized report, wrong PID/ctime/parent, missing release, target exec failure and fsync failure controls still refuse.

Record separate parent launch-start/ready/register/release/wait-return/fsync boundaries in a source-bound future instrument before attributing startup or hashing cost; keep observer call budgets unchanged.

Only after source-bound equivalence controls and a separately frozen bounded engineering protocol, compare startup candidates on fixed workloads with failures retained. No live probe or new qualification is authorized/executed by this diagnosis.

limits: One stopped run, ten sequential observations, one host/configuration, increasing prefix population and elapsed time confounded. No independent samples or causal growth estimate.
No fsync-only, site-import-only, daemon-SHA-only or target-exec-only measured duration; subtractive envelopes cannot manufacture them.
No extrapolated performance claim, successful full equivalent load, new formal prospective qualification decision, fresh case or seed.
